comment: Tools/Build/risky_merge.py: the ONE definition of a risky merge (Garrett, 2026-11-17: 'as long as we have a way to flag the risky stuff, and get sign off after the fact I would rather move as fast as we can'). A merge is risky when it matches any category below. Each category says whether a hit queues a sign-off entry to the signer's /approve list ('queue') or only labels the PR ('label'). Globs are fnmatch patterns on repo paths; 'content' categories also need a changed line matching the regex. Change this file, not the script, to widen or narrow what counts.
label: risky-merge

categories.name: merged past a review rule (no approving review)
categories.why: Every merge into bleeding-edge since 2026-11-16 went in with no approving review (109 of 109 checked), so a bypass alone labels the PR; it queues an entry only together with another category.

categories.name: shared AI code every AI hull runs
vessel kit numbers (abilities, stats, element maps, hull prefabs)
an area another person owns (Docs/TEAM.json owners)
a swim lane someone else occupies (approvals.py check exit 2)
